Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back to the run-chase! The Australian players are out there in the middle. Suzie Bates and Sophie Devine are the openers for New Zealand Women. Megan Schutt to start with the ball. Here we go...
The Run Chase....

New Zealand Women bowled well in the last few overs but they would be disappointed with their bowling performance overall especially after getting rid of Mooney in the first over. Lea Tahuhu was the pick of the bowlers for them and got the breakthroughs everytime the game seemed to be running away from the Kiwis. She took three wickets and Amelia Kerr too was brilliant with three wickets to her name and played a big part in restricting Aussies under 180 here. Now, it is time for the New Zealand Women batters to step up and take on this powerful Australian bowling line-up and it would be interesting chase if they do get to a good start in the Powerplay. Stay tuned for the run-chase!

Alyssa Healy is up for a quick chat. She says that it can be enough if they bowl well enough and hopes that their bowlers can do the job. Adds that she didn't know how much she had in her and they tried to maintain the intensity right throughout but weren't able to do so. Adds that Lea Tahuhu got a bit of indifferent bounce but the key here is to bowl at the stumps. Mentions that every game in the World Cup matters and they like playing against their neighbours.

Australia lost the prolific Mooney in the very first over but Lanning and Healy batted with intent and stitched together a brisk stand of 70 runs. That set the platform for the rest of the batters to capitalise and though Lanning departed after a well-made 41, Healy continued and found an able partner in Perry after Gardner departed without making much of an impact. Healy scored fifty and Perry smashed 40 off 22 balls to put more pressure on the Kiwis. They lost their way a bit at the backend but still managed to get a very healthy score on the board.

A good little comeback from New Zealand in the last few overs but it is still a pretty strong batting performance from the Aussies. They have managed to cross 170 here and New Zealand would need to be at their best with the bat to chase this total down.

FOUR! A streaky boundary to end the innings but Darcie Brown and Australia Women will take it. Full and angling into leg stump, Brown backs away and looks to go over covers but ends up slicing it over cover-point. The ball trickles away into the fence and Australia Women fisnish with 173/9!
Back of a length around off, Darcie Brown backs away and plays it uppishly over backward point for a couple of runs.
Darcie Brown is the last batter in!

OUT! CAUGHT! Excellent bowling this from Jess Kerr and New Zealand Women have done extremely well to pull things back. Slower one, full and around off, Tahlia McGrath stays deep in her crease and looks to loft it over extra cover. There's not much pace on the ball and McGrath ends up chipping it toward extra cover where Sophie Devine takes a simple catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Sophie Devine b Jess Kerr

Commentary.Commentary: Well bowled! Nagging length around off, Tahlia McGrath looks to shuffle across and pull but the ball skids on and beats the bat.
Fullish length, pushed wider of the off stump, Megan Schutt walks across and slogs it to deep mid-wicket for one.
A length baall angling into leg stump, Tahlia McGrath backs away and hits it down to long off for a run.
Megan Schutt is the next batter in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Another one bites the dust and Australia Women lose their eigth wicket. Hayley Jensen rolls her fingers over the ball and bowls it on a length down leg. Alana King gets a bit low and looks to slog it away over the mid-wicket fence. King only manages to loft it towards deep square leg where Lea Tahuhu settles under it and takes it safely just inside the ropes.
Commentary.Howout: c Lea Tahuhu b Hayley Jensen

Commentary.Commentary: Tahlia McGrath tries to back away but Hayley Jensen does well to follow here. McGrath pushes it toward mid off and picks up a single.
Fuller in length and outside off, Alana King lofts it down to long off and turns the strike over.
Pitched up around off, Alana King pushes it to the left of the bowler.
Back of a length around off, this is punched off the back foot toward cover for one.
FOUR! Exquisite timing! Full and around off, Tahlia McGrath bacsk away and creams it through the cover region for a boundary.
Alana King walks out to the middle now.

OUT! TAKEN! Straight to the fielder and Maddy Green jujst about holds on. Amelia Kerr serves a full toss on middle and leg and the ball just dips on the batter a bit. Jess Jonassen looks for the slog-sweep but doesn't quite swing freely and ends up hitting it flat toward deep mid-wicket. Maddy Green there almost spills the catch but manages to hand on and Amelia Kerr picks up her third wicket of the game. Jess Jonassen is out for a duck and New Zealand Women finishing on a high here.
Commentary.Howout: c Maddy Green b Amelia Kerr

Commentary.Commentary: On a nagging length on leg stump, Jess Jonassen watchfully keeps it out.
Jess Jonassen walks out to the middle.

OUT! LBW! Ellyse Perry pre-meditates and shuffles right across the stumps. Amelia Kerr sees this and bowls it flatter on the stumps. Perry falls over as she looks to pull the ball off one knee and misses. The ball thuds into the pads and there is a loud appeal for lbw and it is given. Perry gets up and reviews. No spike on UltraEdge and Ball Tracking shows it is crashing into middle. Amelia Kerr gets the wicket and Perry departs after a quickfire knock.
SIX! Clean strike! Tossed up around off, Ellyse Perry goes inside out and lofts it all the way over the wide long off fence for a maximum.
Shorter and outside off, Perry fails to get it past cover-point.
Tosses it up now, full and outside off, Ellyse Perry steps out and pushes it toward cover.
Shorter one, worked away to deep square leg for another single.
Back of a length and on the body, Tahlia McGrath works it away through mid-wicket for a run.
WIDE! On a good length and just angling down leg, wide called.
Can Australia Women reach 180 from here?
Full and straight, driven down to long on for a single.

OUT! RUN OUT! A horrible mix up in the middle and Grace Harris has to depart. Hayley Jensen bowls it full and on leg stump, Grace Harris flicks it away through mid-wicket for one and looks for the second right away. Harris is halfway down the track when Ellyse Perry sends her back. Lea Tahuhu in the deep fires in a wide throw at the bowler's end but Jensen does well to latch onto it and under-arm it onto the stumps before Harris got back. Tahlia McGrath is the next batter in.
FOUR! Perfectly timed and in the gap. Fullish length on the pads, Grace Harris clips it away in between deep square leg and deep mid-wicket for yet another boundary.

FOUR! Unlucky for the bowler! This is very full and angling into the toes, Grace Harris just about manages to get some bat on it and the ball runs off the inside edge past short fine leg for a boundary.
On the pads and this is tucked away behind square leg for a couple of runs. Excellent running.
SIX! All the way! On a good length around off, Ellyse Perry shuffles down the track and holds her shape before whacking the ball over the wide long off fence for a biggie.
The call is for two but they settle for the single. Good length on the stumps, worked away in front of mid-wicket for one.
FOUR! Short and wide outside off, there to be hit and Grace Harris just frees her arms before thrashing it away over backward point for a boundary.
A length ball around middle, just nipping back in. Grace Harris looks to tentatively block it but gets a faint inside edge onto the back leg.
Grace Harris is the next batter in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Lea Tahuhu has done it again! Tahuhu comes back into the attack ans starts with a pitched up delivery around leg stump. Alyssa Healy backs away and looks to loft it straight down the ground. Healy is a bit early in the swing and ends up just lifting it down to long on where Maddy Green moves to her left and takes it safely. Healy departs after a fine knock and Tahuhu gets the breakthrough New Zealand Women desperately needed.
Commentary.Howout: c Maddy Green b Lea Tahuhu

Commentary.Commentary: Lea Tahuhu is back for her final over!
Well bowled! Jess Kerr takes a bit of pace off the ball and bowls it a bit fuller on the fourth stump line. Ellyse Perry looks to drive inside-out but is well beaten.
Goes full and wide now, Ellyse Perry just strokes it to the fielder at cover.
Good length around middle and leg, flciked away through square leg for a single.
FOUR! Slapped away! Just a fraction short and outside off, Healy cuts it hard and past point for a boundary.

FIFTY up for Alyssa Healy and she just loves playing against this opposition. This is her fourth T20I 50 against New Zealand Women. Good length angling into the pads, this is worked away in front of mid-wicket for a couple of runs. She will now look to up the ante even further.
Nicely bowled! Alyssa Healy backs away a long way past leg stump and Jess Kerr follows her with a full delivery. Healy looks to drive but misses.

FOUR! Oh, no! Hannah Rowe has made a mess of it. This is tossed up outside off, Ellyse Perry drives it firmly through extra cover and Rowe at wide long off just overruns the ball and Perry picks up yet another boundary. Australia Women in a commanding position at the moment.
FOUR! Nicely done! Slows it up now and bowls it a bit shorter outside off. Ellyse Perry waits for it and edges it with soft hands fine of the fielder at short third man for a boundary.
Flatter one around off, tapped away toward cover for one.
FOUR! Finds the gap! This is fired in outside off, Alyssa Healy pre-meditates and shuffles across the of stump before whipping it away into the vacant square leg fence.
Lofted but lands safely. Tossed up outside off, Alyssa Healy steps out and lifts it over the cover region for a couple of runs.
Shorter in length and around off, pushed away in front of point for a single.
FOUR! Cheekily done! Fullish length outside off, Alyssa Healy shuffles right across the stumps and ramps it off the toe end of the bat past short fine leg for a boundary.
Excellent work in the deep from Fran Jonas. Full and outside off, this is sliced away over backward point. Jonas hunts it down and just manages to pull it back in. Just the brace then.
FOUR! Bang! Good length around off, Alyssa Healy flat-bats it over mid off for a boundary.
Short and wide, cut away to sweeper cover for a single.
Back of a length and around off, Ellyse Perry shuffles across and muscles it over wide mid on for a couple of runs.
On a hard length and on the pads, this iw worked away leg side for a run.
Flatter again aoutside the off stump, Ellyse Perry looks to sweep but misses out.
This is bowled around off, Alyssa Healy goes for the sweep but gets an inside edge toward short third man for one.
Flatter and on the pads, tucked away 'round the corner for a single.

Nicely bowled! This is the wrong 'un, around off and turning back in sharply. Ellyse Perry gets pushed onto the back foot and gets squared up. The ball pings here on the back leg but there isn't much of an appeal. Ball Tracking shows that had New Zealand Women reviewed, Perry would have been sent back. A golden opportunity missed by the Kiwis.

Firmly struck! Looped up full and around middle, Ellyse Perry steps out and converts it into a full toss before drilling it straight back past the bowler. Hannah Rowe at long on runs to her left and keeps it down to a couple.
This is dragged down by Amelia Kerr around off, Ellyse Perry rocks back and pulls it down to deep square leg for a couple of runs.
On a good length outside off, Perry reaches out and taps it in front of cover-point.
Banged into the deck and at the stumps, Ellyse Perry latches onto it and forces the pull over mid-wicket for three runs.
FOUR! A gift first ball for Ellyse Perry. This is full and on the pads, Perry clips it away fine and the ball runs away into the fine leg fence.
Ellyse Perry is the next batter in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Great move to bring back Lea Tahuhu and Ashleigh Gardner walks back for a low score. Tahuhu pitches it up on the pads, looking for the away swinger and Gardner tries to tuck it away. Gardner closes the face of the bat early and ends up getting a leading edge. The ball lobs up around backward point where Eden Carson takes a simple catch. Australia Women are now three down.
Commentary.Howout: c Eden Carson b Lea Tahuhu

Commentary.Commentary: Good length, angling into middle and leg, Gardner works it off the inner half of the bat through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Beaten! Length ball outside off and the ball moves away nicely from the right-hander. Ashleigh Gardner looks to come forward and drive but the ball goes past the outside edge.
WIDE! A length ball, slinging down the leg side and a wide is called.
Lea Tahuhu (2-0-14-1) is back on.
Tossed up on off. Healy skips down the track and drives it to the cover fielder. End of a fine over from Amelia Kerr!
Touch shorter and on off. Ashleigh Gardner works it to deep square leg for a single.

Drinks break! With the fall of Meg Lanning, drinks are called onto the field. After losing Beth Mooney really early, Meg Lanning and Alyssa Healy did well to steady the ship and just when Lanning looked in complete control, she was undone by Amelia Kerr. New Zealand Women are right in the contest but with Australia's tall batting order, the Kiwis will need regular wickets. Let's see how things pan out. Also, Ashleigh Gardner comes in to bat next.

OUT! BOWLED! Amelia Kerr strikes! This is a crucial breakthrough and a superb knock from the Australian skipper comes to an end. Kerr is a very clever bowler and she shows it once again here. Bowls it touch short, close to off and it is a googly at 75 kph. Lanning makes room to cut it as she fails to pick the googly and the ball goes onto knock the off pole. Can New Zealand Women capitalise on this opening now?
Bowls it full and on middle. Healy skips down the track and drives it to long on for a single.
Bowls it fuller and on off. Healy makes room and drives it to the extra cover fielder. The fielder there misfields and two runs are taken.
Tossed up and outside off. Healy tries to sweep it but misses.
Amelia Kerr (1-0-7-0) comes from the opposite end now.
FOUR! Lanning is finding boundaries with ease here! This is flatter and outside off. Lanning skips down the track and smashes it through covers for a boundary.
On middle and quicker. Lanning works it to deep square leg for a couple.
FOUR! Powerful shot! Carson bowls it on off. Lanning skips down the track, takes it on full and whips it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Tossed up and outside off. Lanning chips it over mid off for a couple.
Short of full length and on middle and leg. Lanning tries to pull it but gets an inside edge onto her pads.
A fuller delivery to start from off. Healy works it to long on for a single.
Youngster Eden Carson has now been tossed the ball.
Another dot to end the over! A full delivery on off. Lanning drills it to wide mid off. Good over, just 2 from it!
Serves it on a length, around off. Lanning pushes it to backward point.
On a length, on middle. Healy works it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
On a length, on leg. Healy makes room and pushes it towards the off side.
Bowls it full and on off. Lanning drives it to long on for a single.
Bowls it on a fullish length swinging into middle and leg. Lanning tries to clip it but misses and gets hit on the pads. Going down the leg though.
Jess Kerr (1-0-13-0) comes back in to replace Fran Jonas.
Loopy delivery on off. Lanning shimmies down the track and hits it off the bounce to left of mid on. Sophie Devine does well to stop it and keeps it to just a single.
Tosses it up and outside off. Healy drives it to sweeper cover for a single.
Bowls it quicker and touch shorter on off. Healy punches it towards the off side.
Goes fuller and on off. Healy sweeps it to square leg.
Shortish and outside off. Lanning slaps it to sweeper cover for a single.

FOUR! Amelia Kerr is greeted with a boundary here! 50 up for the Aussies! Shortish and on leg. Lanning gets a slight touch on it as she tries to pull it. The ball runs away past short fine leg for a boundary.
Amelia Kerr is now brought into the attack.

FOUR! Healy ends the Powerplay with a boundary and Australia Women are 47 for 1 after 6 overs! This is flatter and quicker on off. Healy makes room, dances down the track and drives it over extra cover for a boundary.
Bowls it fuller and on off. Healy drives it to the extra cover fielder.
Fuller and quicker on off. Lanning pushes it to long off for a single.
Touch short again on off. Lanning punches it to the cover-point fielder.
FOUR! Short and wide outside off. Lanning is very strong in that area and she cuts it through backward point for a boundary. Can't bowl there to Lanning!
Flatter and quicker on off. Lanning makes room and punches it to covers.
Fran Jonas (1-0-6-0) is brought back to bowl the final over of the Powerplay.
Back of a length, on middle. Lanning pulls it to deep square leg for just a single this time.
FOUR! The pressure was building with four dot balls but this boundary will take it away now. Touch shorter on off; Lanning pulls it to deep square leg for a boundary.
On the shorter side and outside off. Lanning punches it to backward point.
Shortish and outside off. Lanning tries to slog it across the line but misses.
On a length and outside off. Lanning punches it to the point fielder.

On a length, on middle. Lanning works it to mid-wicket and sets off for a single. Healy is ball watching and sends Lanning back. Lanning puts in a dive to get back in her crease and makes her ground as the throw comes in from mid-wicket and the keeper knocks over the stumps.
Hayley Jensen comes into the attack now.
FOUR! These are not good signs for the Kiwis! Healy is looking in good touch here. Shortish and on off. Healy pulls it without much fuss towards the square leg fence for a boundary.
FOUR! Up and over! Kerr bowls an overpitched delivery on off. Healy holds her shape and lifts it over mid off for a boundary.
On a length and outside off. Healy guides it towards short third man.
Shortish and on off. Healy pulls it to the mid-wicket fielder.
Bowls it full and on middle. Lanning drives it to mid on for a single.

FOUR! An outside edge produces a boundary this time! Wonderful seam position bowls a fullish delivery on off. Lanning tries to defend it off the front foot. However, the ball catches the outside edge and runs away to third man for a boundary.
A first change in the bowling as Jess Kerr comes into the attack.
FOUR! Poor delivery and punished! A full toss on the pads. It is there for Healy to hit and she glances it through the mid-wicket region for a boundary.
Goes fuller and on off. Lanning drives it to mid off for a single.
FOUR! Lanning with a powerful flick shot! This is fullish and on middle and leg. Lanning gets across a bit and whips it off her pads towards the backward square leg fence for a boundary.
Again a tight line, on off. Lanning fends it towards the point fielder.
Lands it on a length, on off. Lanning punches it to the cover fielder. New Zealand have started well here.
Again a full delivery on middle. Lanning pushes it to the cover region.
WIDE! Goes full and down the leg side. Lanning tries to flick it but misses.
Serves it fuller on off. Lanning with a beautiful drive to long off for a single.
Nicely bowled! A flatter and quicker one on off. Lanning drives it to the cover fielder.
Touch shorter and slower through the air on leg. Healy skips down the track and works it to mid-wicket for a single.
A flatter delivery and quicker on off. Healy blocks it out.
FOUR! In the gap and first boundary for Australia Women! Touch short on off. Healy makes room and cuts it through cover-point for a boundary.
Shortish and on off. Healy goes back and punches it to covers.
Fran Jonas to operate from the opposite end.
A fullish delivery, around off to end the over. Healy goes for the drive but gets a thick outside edge to third man for a single. End of a riveting first over!
On a length and around off. Lanning steers it towards third man for a single.
Skipper Meg Lanning walks in at number 3.

OUT! Oh, brilliant! What a catch from young Eden Carson at point! Beth Mooney departs for a duck and this is just the start New Zealand Women needed! On a length and outside off. Bit of shape away from Mooney and she drives it away from her body. The ball goes off the outside edge towards the right of point where Eden Carson dives full length and takes a stunner. Lea Tahuhu strikes in the first over!
Commentary.Howout: c Eden Carson b Lea Tahuhu

Commentary.Commentary: An overpitched delivery and outside off. Mooney drives it to the cover fielder.
WIDE! On the shorter side again but spills it down the leg side. Mooney tries to clip it but misses.

Healy and Australia Women are underway in this World Cup! On the shorter side, around off. Some extra bounce and Healy just about manages to guide it towards third man as she rides the bounce and takes a single.
Lea Tahuhu starts off with a very full delivery on middle. Bit of shape into the batter and Healy fends it out towards the leg side.

The pre-game formalities are done and it is now time to get the play underway. The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of New Zealand Women who are seen in a huddle. Alyssa Healy and Beth Mooney are all-set to open the innings for Australia Women. Lea Tahuhu has the new ball in hand an is ready to get going. Let's play...

Just a few minutes left now for the start of play but first, the two teams will line up for their respective national anthems. It will be national anthem of New Zealand first, followed by the national anthem of Australia.
New Zealand Women (Playing XI) - Sophie Devine (C), Suzie Bates, Bernadine Bezuidenhout (WK), Amelia Kerr, Maddy Green, Hannah Rowe, Hayley Jensen, Lea Tahuhu, Jess Kerr, Eden Carson, Fran Jonas.
Australia Women (Playing XI) - Alyssa Healy (WK), Beth Mooney, Meg Lanning (C), Ashleigh Gardner, Ellyse Perry, Tahlia McGrath, Grace Harris, Jess Jonassen, Alana King, Megan Schutt, Darcie Brown.
TOSS - The coin goes up in the air and Sophie Devine calls it right. New Zealand Women have decided to BOWL first.

The first game on Super Saturday which was played between England Women and West Indies Women at the very same venue has concluded and it is the English women who were able to chase down 136 runs for victory with 7 wickets in hand. Now, it is time to focus on this game and we aren't that far away from the toss and team news. Stay tuned.

With the Women’s T20 World Cup 2023 well and truly underway, the attention of the cricketing world is now on this mega event to see which team is able to crown themselves champions. The spotlight is currently on match number 3 for the Group 1 clash which sees the reigning champions begin their title defense against New Zealand Women at the Boland Park in Paarl. Australia Women are clear favorites as they hunt for their sixth trophy and come into this tournament in good form beating India Women 4-1 away and Pakistan Women 2-0 at home. They won their first warm-up match against India Women comprehensively but suffered an astonishing defeat against Ireland Women in the second game. New Zealand Women beat Bangladesh Women 3-0 in their last T20I series but enter the competition with poor preparations as they lost both their warm-up matches. They were runners-up in the first two editions and will look to take their form from 2022 when they won 10 out of the 14 games into the tournament. Australia women have been at the top of the T20I rankings since winning the last edition and lost just one game last year via a super over. The team will be led by Meg Lanning who returns after a five-month break and they have a potent opening partnership with Beth Mooney and Alyssa Healy. They have a dangerous middle order comprising Tahlia McGrath, Ashleigh Gardner, Grace Harris, and Ellyse Perry. Megan Schutt and Darcie Brown form a lethal pace bowling combination and Alana King will fulfill the spin bowling duties. New Zealand Women will be captained by Sophie Devine who will rely heavily on veteran all-rounder Suzie Bates and the talented Amelia Kerr. Bernadine Bezuidenhout has been picked as the wicket-keeper and returns to the squad after a hiatus of two years with Brooke Halliday also returning from a hand injury. The Under-19 World Cup squad members, Georgia Plimmer and Fran Jonas will also be a part of the side as they look to impress at the senior level. Will Australia Women begin the hunt for their third consecutive title with a win? Or will New Zealand Women pull off an upset early in the tournament? We will find out soon.
